text:
ana: FYI bringing tethys-v2 through int8 showed a small but consistent degradation on multilang sets that mix CJK + Arabic/Persian scripts. small sample shows token boundary shifts around middle-dot/hyphen combos :thinking_face:
mina: Oof. Which eval and numbers?
nana: quick summary: JP/AR validation cluster, 8.5k examples. BLEU down 3.8 points, chrF -0.04 overall. failures heavily concentrated on lines that interleave Han + Arabic + katakana and use mixed punctuation.
dmitri: Can you paste a minimal repro string and token dumps?
nana: paste below (keeps some punctuation variants):
```
Source: 北京·القاهرةテスト・チェック—مثال
FP16 detok: 北京·القاهرةテスト・チェック—مثال
INT8 detok: 北京3·القاهرة-テスト・チェック-مثال
```
(note: U+00B7 vs U+30FB vs U+183 used here as example, em-dash U+2014 vs hyphen U+002D. also stray U+001F control sneaked in from some legacy source)
dmitri: ran our tokenizer harness on the exact string. tokens differ before model step: 
```
FP16 tokens: ["北京","\u00B7","القاهرة","\u2014","テスト","・","チェック","—","مثال"]
INT8 tokens: ["北京","\u183","\u00B7","القاهرة","-","テスト","・","チェック","-","مثال"]
```
so there is a token seam shift, plus an extra obscure control code folding to U+183 in one path. that would explain detok + alignment drift.
mina: Are we sure it's quantization and not different tokenizer versions? we ship tokenizer tables in the runtime artifacts, but int8 bringup also switched to a trimmed vocabulary file for memory.
dmitri: good point. two orthogonal changes: smaller vocab pack + quant kernel that uses different byte-alignment. both can influence serialization of input normalization in our artifact build step.
ci-bot: test-run tethys-v2-int8-smoke 4941001150: bleu_base=21.3, bleu_int8=17.5, chrf_base=0.487, chrf_int8=0.443, regression_count=612, top-pattern="cjk+arabic+punct-seams"
ana: Hypotheses: (A) preprocessing normalizer behaves differently in trimmed vocab build; (B) a locale-dependent mapping (we default to zh locale for CJK, ar for Arabic) has a fallback bug that toggles mapping of middle dots and dashes; (C) quantized tokenizer binary serialization introduced a byte-ordering issue for control-range chars.
mina: Quick mitigation idea: deterministic punctuation canonicalization at ingress (NFKC + explicit mapping table) before tokenization so tokenizer input is identical across builds. cheap and low-risk.
dmitri: Agreed. also add a small post-tokenization sanity: canonical_ids = normalize_then_tokenize(s); assert(len(set(sha256(token_ids_fp16) , sha256(token_ids_int8))) == 1) for canonical inputs. Put a handful of tricky fixtures under tests/locale/hybrid_punct_cases.txt
ana: I prototyped a tiny normalizer: 
```
# canonicalize punctuation and control chars
s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
# map common variants to canonical forms
s = s.replace('\u00B7', '\u30FB')  # middle dot -> katakana mid dot
s = s.replace('\u2014', '\u002D')  # em-dash -> ASCII hyphen
s = re.sub('[\x00-\x1F]', '', s)   # drop control chars
```
mina: Please don't silently drop controls without logging; replace with U+FFFD or strip? Some corpora rely on them. maybe we just normalize to space and log counts to metrics.
dmitri: good catch. use replacement and metric. Also we must ensure the same canonicalizer runs in hosted, dedicated and private tokenizers. add a config flag tokenize.canonical_punct=true and default off for private until we can roll it out.
ci-bot: canary-plan created: 4941001170 -> route 3% int8 traffic with canonicalizer on. will collect BLEU/chrF deltas and token-stability traces.
nana: owners: ana -> canonicalizer PR, dmitri -> tokenizer unit tests + fixture file, mina -> coordinate canary + metrics. I'll push a short repro bench and attach to the PR.
mina: if canonicalization doesn't fix >95% of regressions we'll escalate to investigating the trimmed vocab pipeline and tokenizer binary serialization.
ana: thanks everyone. ping me if your PRs need extra test data. :rocket:
